title: The Savior overturns an unlawful doctrine
english: In this Christ himself overturned an unlawful doctrine. For some people supposed that sinning souls are sent from heaven into a body for the sake of punishment, and that sometimes the soul is pre-existing by itself apart from the body.
translator_notes: The Greek text may be a fragment, as it appears to start and end mid-sentence.
The translation is literal, and the sentence end is marked with a trailing … to indicate a cut.
baehrens: PG 65; Fragmenta in Joannem (Khazarzar) u01 rem early
orientation: The author is introducing the fragment's comment on John 3, where Christ himself is said to overturn an unlawful doctrine.

title: The error of souls joined to bodies for sins
english: Sometimes the soul pre-exists by itself, and at other times it is joined to bodies as punishment for its own sins, so that a woman can conceive only when some soul sins. Christ destroys this error.
translator_notes: The Greek text appears to be a fragment, cut off at the end. The translation is literal, but the sentence is incomplete.
baehrens: PG 65; Fragmenta in Joannem (Khazarzar) u01 rem mid
orientation: Theophilus is describing the unlawful doctrine that Christ overturned, explaining how its adherents thought souls relate to bodies.

title: Christ answers the question and destroys the error
english: When Christ was asked about this error, he was saying: "Neither this man sinned nor his parents, but this happened so that the works of God might be revealed" (John 3).
translator_notes: The Greek text appears to be a fragment, starting mid-sentence. The translation is literal, without attempting to complete the missing words.
baehrens: PG 65; Fragmenta in Joannem (Khazarzar) u01 rem close
orientation: The author has just described the unlawful doctrine that souls are sent into bodies for punishment, and now quotes Christ's answer to the question about whose sin caused the condition.
